A Natural Silver Reaction
Dark spots occur naturally over time when silver is
exposed to air or different water qualities. This is a
common characteristic of genuine silver.

baking soda with a few drops of water, gently scrub, and
rinse to restore shine instantly.

1. Before Your First Day Back

Check what workplace pumping

3. Have A Backup Plan
Know one backup option if your pump
does not cooperate.
• Consider hand expression or a backup
manual pump.
Keep extra pump parts at work or in
your bag.

• Pump + charger or power source

口

BACK-TO-WORK Pumping Checklist
A simple one-page plan for
your workday pumping routine
Momcozy × Aeroflow Breastpumps | Melissa Kotlen, RN, IBCLC I
Sarah Van Zandt, IBCLC, PMH-C
1. Before Your First Day Back
Test your pumping setup before the first
workweek.
口
Confirm that pumping feels comfortable
and your flange fit works for you.
Know your pump parts, charger/power
source, and basic setup.
Identify when and where you can
realistically pump during your workday.
Plan around your baby's usual feeding
pattern, your time apart, and your
available work breaks.
Check what workplace pumping
protections and space may apply to you.
3. Have A Backup Plan
Know one backup option if your pump
does not cooperate.
• Consider hand expression or a backup
manual pump.
Keep extra pump parts at work or in
your bag.
L
J
Carry a spare charger or power cord.
If safe milk storage is not available,
keep prioritizing comfort and regular
milk removal.
2. Pack Your Pump-At-Work Bag
• Pump + charger or power source
Correct-fit flanges or inserts
Bottles or milk storage bags
L
Cooler bag + frozen ice packs, if needed
Spare parts for the pieces most likely to
get lost or fail
口
Labels or a simple tracking system
Nursing pads + an extra shirt
Water + snack
4. Keep The Routine Flexible
口
Aim for regular milk removal—not
perfect timing
If baby feeds before you leave, adjust
the timing of your first pump.
If meetings or breaks shift, adjust the
remaining sessions as needed.
A shorter session can still provide some
milk removal and relief when time is
limited.
Avoid making skipped milk removals
your regular pattern.
Keep it simple: the best routine is one you can actually repeat on a real workday.

manual pump.

口

perfect timing

Breaking Barriers: Insights and Solutions from Leaders in Breastfeeding Advocacy
To celebrate Breastfeeding Awareness Month, we ve interviewed leaders from top organizations
like ACNM, The Baby Academy, Pumpspotting, Mama Glow, and NAPS. They share insights on
breastfeeding barriers, expert advice, future advocacy goals, and words of encouragement for
current and future breastfeeding moms. Join us in highlighting these inspiring voices dedicated to
empowering mothers and fostering a supportive breastfeeding community.
About: NAPS is a trusted parenting partner, offering online, nurse-led support, education, and
coaching from pregnancy to preschool.（放在专家图片下
方）
What do you believe is the biggest barrier to successful breastfeeding in your
field?
From society to social media, there is immense pressure on mothers which, while sometimes well-
intentioned. can create barriers to successful breastfeedina. The pervasive expectation that "breas
is best" can lead to feelings of guilt and inadequacy for those who struggle with breastfeeding or
choose alternative feeding methods. This pressure is fueled by societal judgment and unsolicited
opinions, creating an environment where mothers feel hesitant to share their feeding choices. This
includes blanket statements and little acknowledgment that every family, every baby, and every
feeding journey is different. What worked for one might not work for another. This lack of support
ana understanding can isolate moners, making it amicult tor unem to seek nelp or aiscuss ineir
experiences openly, further complicating their feeding journey and overall well-
being.
What solutions or advice would you offer to overcome this

and climate all matter. The goal is to
